note: Franky's notebook. Written by the duck itself (the model's weights never change). tries = attempts the note was shown in, wins = how many of those succeeded.

knowledge.text: The beak only takes the banana if its middle is within 7 cm of the beak tip.
The banana's long side must be within 30 degrees of lying across the beak for the beak to grab it.
Attempts failed even when the banana was 0.09 m away (Step 9), showing distance alone is insufficient for a grab.
If the specific target container (e.g., green box) is not found, searching for a generic type (e.g., box) may lead to the wrong container.
Dropping the banana at 0.28 m distance from the target container does not ensure it is inside the container.

skills.text: Approach the banana until it is within 7 cm and oriented across the beak (within 30 degrees) before closing the beak.
Always verify the banana's orientation relative to the beak tip before attempting to pick it up.
After dropping the banana, verify its location relative to the container to ensure it is fully inside.
When approaching a container, measure the distance and bearing to align the drop point correctly.
